sourceHtml:
When you call an open-weight model through an API, several providers may serve it at different precisions, such as 16-bit bf16, 8-bit fp8 or 4-bit fp4. The precision can affect both the answers and the price. LLM quantization creates these versions by storing a model’s weights in fewer bits, so the model needs less memory and hardware, at some cost in accuracy.

This post explains the formats and reports what we measured on OpenRouter on October 20, 2026, across 1,455 provider endpoints and six endpoints serving Qwen3.8 27B. On our test, we didn’t detect an accuracy difference between fp8, fp4 and fp16, so the precision label alone didn’t predict accuracy. Lower precision was usually cheaper, but not for every model.

TL;DR

  • We didn’t detect an accuracy difference between fp8, fp4 and fp16 on our 240 scored tasks. All six endpoints scored between 98.3% and 99.2%.

  • On 40 more multiplication tasks, one fp4 endpoint scored lowest, by a gap too small to rule out chance.

  • 8-bit was cheaper than 16-bit for 14 of the 24 models served at both, and more expensive for 7. 4-bit was cheaper than 8-bit for 26 of 33.

  • provider.quantizations pins the precision you get. List every precision you’d accept, so the router has more than one endpoint to fall back to.

What is LLM quantization?

LLM quantization means storing a large language model’s numbers with fewer bits than it was trained with. Most LLMs today use FP16 or BF16, which are 16-bit formats. fp8 halves the memory each weight takes, and fp4 or int4 quarters it, so the same GPU holds a bigger model or serves more requests. The cost is accuracy, because each weight is rounded to the nearest value the smaller format can store.

FormatBits per weightWeights for a 27B modelWhere you see it
bf16 / fp161654 GBThe precision most models are released in
fp8827 GBThe most common labeled precision on OpenRouter
fp4, nvfp4, mxfp4, int4413.5 GBCheaper endpoints, local runs, some lab releases

These figures cover weights only. A running model also needs memory for its KV cache, the stored attention state for each token in the context.

There are two main types of quantization. Post-training quantization converts a finished model’s weights. It can be dynamic, computing the range of each activation at run time, or static, computing those ranges in advance by passing sample data through the model. Quantization-aware training simulates the rounding during training so the weights learn to tolerate it. The Hugging Face Optimum concept guide explains both, and the Transformers quantization overview covers the quantization methods you can run yourself.

fp8 vs bf16: what’s the difference?

Floating-point formats split their bits between a sign, an exponent and a mantissa. The exponent sets the range of values, and the mantissa sets how finely values within that range are resolved.

bf16 has 1 sign bit, 8 exponent bits and 7 mantissa bits, so it has the same range as 32-bit fp32 with less precision. fp16 splits its 16 bits as 5 exponent and 10 mantissa bits. The OCP 8-bit floating point spec defines two fp8 encodings, E4M3 (4 exponent bits, 3 mantissa bits) and E5M2 (5 exponent bits, 2 mantissa bits). fp8 gives up both range and precision, so quantized models store a scale factor per tensor or per block of weights. MXFP4 shares one scale across each block of 32 values, and NVFP4 uses one fp8 scale per 16 values.

For an API user, fp8 vs bf16 shows up as a different label and price on the same model. In our test, we didn’t detect a difference between the three fp8 endpoints and the fp16 endpoint.

How much quality is lost with fp8 and fp4?

We didn’t detect a quality loss at fp8 or fp4 in our test. All six endpoints scored between 98.3% and 99.2%, and a test this size can’t rule out a gap of a point or two.

We ran 280 tasks with exact answers through qwen/qwen3.8-27b, pinned to six endpoints. Cerebras serves it at fp16. Parasail, CoreWeave and AkashML serve it at fp8, and Darkbloom and ModelRun serve it at fp4. Each request set provider.only, quantizations and allow_fallbacks: false, so it could only reach the endpoint we named, at temperature 0 with reasoning off. The tasks were multi-step arithmetic with working, Python programs to trace, lists of 20 to 30 numbers to sort, a key to find among 240 or 1,200 entries (about 4,000 and 20,000 tokens), and a four-step lookup chain through about 9,000 tokens. We generated every task, so each has an exact answer and no judge is needed. Another 40 tasks asked for the product of two four-digit numbers with no working, scored separately.

Task familyTasksfp16 Cerebrasfp8 Parasailfp8 CoreWeavefp8 AkashMLfp4 Darkbloomfp4 ModelRun
Arithmetic with working50484948494950
Short code traces50505050505050
Long code traces30302929292928
Sorting 20 to 30 numbers30302929292930
Recall at 4,000 tokens20202020202020
Recall at 20,000 tokens20202020202020
Four-hop recall40394040403940
Total24098.8%98.8%98.3%98.8%98.3%99.2%
Multiplication, no working40303331322630

Source: OpenRouter, Qwen3.8 27B, October 20, 2026. The 95% confidence intervals on the totals run from 95.8% to 99.8%, and all six overlap.

No task family separated the precisions. Each endpoint missed at most two tasks in any family, and the misses were ordinary slips, such as a number dropped from a sorted list. The fp8 endpoints disagreed with each other on 2 to 5 of the 240 tasks, and the two fp4 endpoints on 4. Darkbloom disagreed with the fp16 and fp8 endpoints most often, on 7 or 8 tasks, yet its total was within half a point of fp16.

The one place a gap showed was multiplication with no working. Darkbloom at fp4 got 26 of 40 products exactly right, against 30 to 33 on the other five endpoints, including 30 on ModelRun at fp4. A two-proportion z-test against the best endpoint (33), a comparison we chose after seeing the results, puts the chance of a gap that large arising with no real difference at about 7.5%, so we can’t call it a precision effect. Wrong products were close at every precision, with the median miss off by less than 0.01%.

We ran all 280 tasks twice on Cerebras, and both runs returned identical text on every task. The small differences between endpoints can come from precision, from each provider’s hardware and inference software, or from run-to-run variation on the other endpoints, and at this size we can’t separate them. Cerebras is the only fp16 endpoint, so fp16 has no second endpoint to compare it with.

This test covers one model, 280 tasks and six endpoints on one day. It doesn’t show that 4-bit is safe for every model or workload, so test your own prompts before you move traffic to a 4-bit endpoint.

Which precision do API providers serve?

fp8 is the most common labeled precision, and most endpoints don’t report a precision at all. We pulled every model’s endpoints from our endpoints API, which returned 1,455 endpoints across 470 models.

Reported precisionEndpointsShare of allShare of labeled
unknown86559.5%
fp834323.6%58.1%
fp41238.5%20.8%
bf16704.8%11.9%
int4201.4%3.4%
nvfp4130.9%2.2%
mxfp4120.8%2.0%
fp1680.5%1.4%
fp3210.1%0.2%

Source: OpenRouter (openrouter.ai/api/v1/models/{author}/{slug}/endpoints), as of October 20, 2026.

610 of the 865 unknown endpoints belong to closed-weight models with no labeled endpoint at all, including every Claude and Gemini model and every OpenAI model except gpt-oss. Of the other 255, 253 are on open-weight models whose providers don’t label precision. Only 54 of the 163 models with a labeled endpoint have a 16-bit one, so for most open-weight models, 8-bit or 4-bit is the only labeled option.

Is a quantized endpoint cheaper?

Usually, but not always. For each model, we compared the cheapest endpoint at each precision, at a blended price of three input tokens to one output token.

ComparisonModelsLower precision cheaperWithin 2%Lower precision more expensiveMedian price ratio
8-bit vs 16-bit2414370.94
4-bit vs 8-bit3326340.76
4-bit vs 16-bit119020.73

Source: OpenRouter endpoints API, list prices including provider discounts, as of October 20, 2026.

Here’s the cheapest endpoint at each precision for five models, in dollars per million blended tokens. Two are exceptions. gpt-oss-120b costs more at 8-bit than at 16-bit, and MiniMax M3 costs more at 4-bit than at 8-bit.

Model16-bit8-bit4-bit
Qwen3.8 27B$0.581$0.342$0.140
Kimi K2.6$1.400$1.079$0.825
Gemma 4 31B$0.205$0.200$0.160
gpt-oss-120b$0.067$0.100$0.060
MiniMax M3None$0.388$0.412

Source: OpenRouter endpoints API, as of October 20, 2026.

The provider affects the price more than the precision does. Where one model has several endpoints at the same precision, the most expensive was a median 1.72 times the cheapest. For Qwen3.8 27B, the ten fp8 endpoints ranged from $0.342 to $1.137 per million blended tokens. To send a request to the cheapest endpoint that passes your precision filter, add :floor to the model slug, as our lowest-cost inference guide explains. With quantizations: [“fp8”], qwen/qwen3.8-27b:floor went to Chutes, the cheapest fp8 endpoint, on both of our tries.

In our test, the cheapest full 280-task run was at fp4 and the most expensive at fp16, but the order in between didn’t follow precision. One run cost $0.58 on Darkbloom (fp4), $0.72 on AkashML (fp8), $0.77 on ModelRun (fp4), $0.81 on Parasail (fp8), $1.19 on CoreWeave (fp8) and $1.24 on Cerebras (fp16). Speed didn’t follow precision either. Cerebras (fp16) and ModelRun (fp4) answered in a median 1.3 and 2.4 seconds, against 8.4 to 15.0 seconds for the other four. Across all endpoints, median 24-hour uptime was 99.8% or higher at every labeled precision except fp32, which has one endpoint.

How do you choose the precision you get?

Check what a model’s endpoints serve, then set provider.quantizations on your requests. A GET to https://openrouter.ai/api/v1/models/qwen/qwen3.8-27b/endpoints returns one entry per endpoint with its quantization, price, context length and uptime. It answered without an API key when we called it, and the model’s providers tab shows the same list. For Qwen3.8 27B it listed 21 endpoints, with one bf16, one fp16, ten fp8, three fp4 and six unknown. Check the count for the precision you want before you pin it, because that count is how many endpoints can take over when one fails.

To keep requests at 8 bits or higher, list the precisions you accept.

import os
import requests

response = requests.post(
    "https://openrouter.ai/api/v1/chat/completions",
    headers={"Authorization": f"Bearer {os.environ['OPENROUTER_API_KEY']}"},
    json={
        "model": "qwen/qwen3.8-27b",
        "messages": [{"role": "user", "content": "What is the capital of Australia? One word."}],
        "reasoning": {"enabled": False},
        "provider": {"quantizations": ["fp8", "bf16", "fp16"]},
    },
    timeout=120,
)
data = response.json()
if "error" in data:
    raise RuntimeError(data["error"])
print(data["provider"], data["choices"][0]["message"]["content"], f'${data["usage"]["cost"]:.6f}')

We ran it three times, and each run printed the same line.

Reka Canberra $0.000007

The provider routing quantization docs list every accepted value and explain how quantizations combines with only, order and sort.

quantizations filters the list of endpoints. We drop every endpoint whose precision isn’t in the list, then load-balance across the rest, weighted toward the lowest price, and fall back to the next endpoint if a provider fails. Nothing in the filter guarantees the same provider each time, so log the response’s provider field if you track quality. The docs also note that fp4 includes mxfp4 and nvfp4, and fp8 includes mxfp8.

Common problems with precision filters and how to fix them

The filter runs before any provider is contacted, so an empty candidate list fails fast. Asking Qwen3.8 27B for int8, which no endpoint serves, returned a 404 in 0.4 seconds.

{"error":{"message":"No endpoints found for the request with quantization: int8. To learn more about provider routing, visit: https://openrouter.ai/docs/guides/routing/provider-selection","code":404,"metadata":{"routing_funnel":[{"step":"Initial Endpoints","endpoint_count":21}],"failed_routing_step":"Filter by Quantization"}}}

The routing_funnel field shows how many endpoints survived each step, and failed_routing_step names the step that left none. {“quantizations”: [“fp8”], “only”: [“cerebras”]} returned the same 404 with quantization: fp8, because Cerebras serves fp16, so the funnel went from 21 endpoints to 1 to none.

The slower failure happens when only one endpoint matches. Cerebras is the only fp16 endpoint for Qwen3.8 27B. During our test, which pinned Cerebras with allow_fallbacks: false, 93 of the first 280 requests failed three times in a row with this error (abridged).

{"message":"Provider returned error","code":429,"metadata":{"raw":"qwen/qwen3.8-27b is temporarily rate-limited upstream. Please retry shortly, or add your own key to accumulate your rate limits: https://openrouter.ai/settings/integrations","provider_name":"Cerebras","limit_source":"upstream_provider_shared_pool","retry_after_seconds":59}}

We retried them until all 280 completed. quantizations: [“fp16”] on its own leaves the same single candidate, so a rate limit there has nowhere else to go. Widening the list to [“fp16”, “bf16”] gave the router a second candidate, and the same request went to DeepInfra.

A provider failure can also arrive with an HTTP 200 status, because we send the status as soon as the provider accepts the request. Check the body for error, not only the status code.

Sort endpoints by quality signals with Exacto

Quantized quality depends “on the method used”, and each provider runs its own inference software, so two endpoints with the same label aren’t guaranteed to match. For requests with tools, Auto Exacto already moves endpoints with lower throughput, tool-calling success rates and benchmark scores to the back of the list. To apply that ordering to requests without tools, add :exacto to the model slug. Exacto ranks endpoints on tool-calling signals, not on accuracy at your task, so run your own prompts against the endpoints you’re considering. How to evaluate LLM provider performance covers how to compare their latency, throughput and uptime.

Frequently asked questions

Is higher or lower quantization better?

More bits keep more of the original model’s precision and take more memory. In our test of Qwen3.8 27B on October 20, 2026, we didn’t detect an accuracy difference between fp8, fp4 and fp16 endpoints on 240 tasks with exact answers. That covers one model on one day, so test 4-bit on your own workload before you commit to it.

Why doesn’t quantization destroy an LLM’s accuracy?

Not all weights matter equally. AWQ found that protecting about 1% of the most important weights greatly reduces quantization error, and LLM.int8() uses mixed precision, keeping outlier values at 16-bit while multiplying more than 99.9% of values in 8-bit. Our test of Qwen3.8 27B can’t show which methods the providers use, but the fp16 endpoint missed 3 of 240 tasks and the fp8 and fp4 endpoints missed 2 to 4.

When should you quantize a model?

Quantize when the model doesn’t fit your hardware at 16-bit, or when you need more throughput from the same GPUs. In our test we didn’t detect a loss at fp8, and fp8 rounds each weight less than 4-bit does, so it’s the smaller step. Test either one on your own tasks first. Through an API you don’t quantize the model yourself. You choose an endpoint on OpenRouter that serves the precision you want, with provider.quantizations.

What does “unknown” quantization mean on a provider?

It means the provider hasn’t reported a precision for that endpoint. On OpenRouter, 865 of 1,455 endpoints were unknown on October 20, 2026, and 610 of those belong to closed-weight models such as Claude and Gemini. unknown is also an accepted value in provider.quantizations, so you can include or exclude those endpoints.

translation.html:
通过 API 调用开放权重模型时，可能有多家提供商以不同精度提供该模型，例如 16 位 bf16、8 位 fp8 或 4 位 fp4。精度可能同时影响回答和价格。LLM 量化通过用更少的位存储模型权重来生成这些版本，使模型所需的内存和硬件资源更少，代价是准确率有所损失。

本文解释这些格式，并报告我们于 2026 年 10 月 20 日在 OpenRouter 上对 1,455 个提供商端点，以及提供 Qwen3.8 27B 的六个端点进行测量的结果。在我们的测试中，未检测到 fp8、fp4 和 fp16 之间的准确率差异，因此仅凭精度标签无法预测准确率。较低精度通常更便宜，但并非每个模型都如此。

要点速览

  • 在 240 道计分任务中，我们未检测到 fp8、fp4 和 fp16 之间的准确率差异。六个端点的得分均在 98.3% 至 99.2% 之间。

  • 在另外 40 道乘法任务中，一个 fp4 端点得分最低，但差距太小，无法排除偶然因素。

  • 在同时提供 8 位和 16 位精度的 24 个模型中，14 个模型的 8 位版本更便宜，7 个更贵。在 33 个模型中，26 个模型的 4 位版本比 8 位更便宜。

  • provider.quantizations 可锁定你获得的精度。列出你能接受的所有精度，让路由器在回退时有不止一个端点可选。

什么是 LLM 量化？

LLM 量化是指用比训练时更少的位来存储大语言模型中的数值。如今大多数 LLM 使用 FP16 或 BF16，这两种都是 16 位格式。fp8 将每个权重占用的内存减半，fp4 或 int4 则将其降至四分之一，因此同一块 GPU 可以容纳更大的模型，或处理更多请求。代价是准确率，因为每个权重都会被舍入到较小格式所能存储的最近数值。

格式每个权重的位数27B 模型的权重大小常见使用场景
bf16 / fp161654 GB大多数模型发布时采用的精度
fp8827 GBOpenRouter 上最常见的已标注精度
fp4, nvfp4, mxfp4, int4413.5 GB更便宜的端点、本地运行、部分实验室发布的模型

这些数字仅涵盖权重。运行中的模型还需要内存来存放 KV 缓存，即上下文中每个 token 已存储的注意力状态。

量化主要有两种类型。训练后量化会转换已训练完成模型的权重。它可以是动态的，在运行时计算每个激活值的范围；也可以是静态的，提前将样本数据输入模型来计算这些范围。量化感知训练则在训练期间模拟舍入，让权重学会适应它。Hugging Face Optimum 概念指南解释了这两种量化方式，Transformers 量化概览则介绍了你可以自行运行的量化方法。

fp8 与 bf16 有什么区别？

浮点格式将位分配给符号、指数和尾数。指数决定数值范围，尾数决定该范围内数值的分辨精细程度。

bf16 有 1 个符号位、8 个指数位和 7 个尾数位，因此它的数值范围与 32 位 fp32 相同，但精度更低。fp16 的 16 位中，指数占 5 位，尾数占 10 位。OCP 8 位浮点规范定义了两种 fp8 编码：E4M3（4 个指数位、3 个尾数位）和 E5M2（5 个指数位、2 个尾数位）。fp8 同时牺牲了范围和精度，因此量化模型会为每个张量或每个权重块存储一个缩放因子。MXFP4 的每个 32 数值块共用一个缩放因子，NVFP4 则为每 16 个数值使用一个 fp8 缩放因子。

对 API 用户而言，fp8 与 bf16 的区别体现为同一模型上不同的标签和价格。在我们的测试中，未检测到三个 fp8 端点与 fp16 端点之间的差异。

fp8 和 fp4 会损失多少质量？

在我们的测试中，未检测到 fp8 或 fp4 带来的质量损失。六个端点的得分均在 98.3% 至 99.2% 之间，而这种规模的测试无法排除一两个百分点的差距。

我们通过 qwen/qwen3.8-27b 运行了 280 道有确切答案的任务，并将请求锁定到六个端点。Cerebras 以 fp16 提供该模型。Parasail、CoreWeave 和 AkashML 以 fp8 提供，Darkbloom 和 ModelRun 以 fp4 提供。每个请求都设置了 provider.only、quantizations 和 allow_fallbacks: false，因此只能访问我们指定的端点，temperature 为 0，且关闭推理。任务包括需写出解题过程的多步算术、跟踪 Python 程序执行、对包含 20 至 30 个数字的列表排序、在 240 或 1,200 个条目中查找一个键（约 4,000 和 20,000 个 token），以及在约 9,000 个 token 中完成四步查找链。所有任务都由我们生成，因此每道任务都有确切答案，无需评判器。另外 40 道任务要求直接给出两个四位数的乘积，不写解题过程，并单独计分。

任务类别任务数fp16 Cerebrasfp8 Parasailfp8 CoreWeavefp8 AkashMLfp4 Darkbloomfp4 ModelRun
写出解题过程的算术50484948494950
短代码执行跟踪50505050505050
长代码执行跟踪30302929292928
对 20 至 30 个数字排序30302929292930
4,000 个 token 中的信息回忆20202020202020
20,000 个 token 中的信息回忆20202020202020
四跳信息回忆40394040403940
合计24098.8%98.8%98.3%98.8%98.3%99.2%
不写解题过程的乘法40303331322630

来源：OpenRouter，Qwen3.8 27B，2026 年 10 月 20 日。总分的 95% 置信区间介于 95.8% 至 99.8% 之间，六个区间均有重叠。

没有任何任务类别能区分这些精度。每个端点在任一类别中最多答错两道任务，错误都是常见失误，例如排序列表中漏掉一个数字。各 fp8 端点彼此在 240 道任务中的 2 至 5 道上给出了不同答案，两个 fp4 端点则在 4 道任务上存在分歧。Darkbloom 与 fp16 和 fp8 端点的答案分歧最频繁，涉及 7 或 8 道任务，但其总分与 fp16 的差距仍在半个百分点以内。

唯一出现差距的是不写解题过程的乘法。fp4 的 Darkbloom 在 40 道任务中完全答对了 26 个乘积，其他五个端点则答对了 30 至 33 个，其中 fp4 的 ModelRun 答对了 30 个。我们在看到结果后选择与最佳端点（答对 33 个）进行双比例 z 检验；结果表明，在不存在真实差异的情况下，出现这么大差距的概率约为 7.5%，因此我们无法将其归因于精度。所有精度下的错误乘积都接近正确值，误差中位数低于 0.01%。

我们在 Cerebras 上将全部 280 道任务运行了两遍，两次运行在每道任务上返回的文本都完全相同。端点之间的微小差异可能来自精度、各提供商的硬件和推理软件，或其他端点不同次运行之间的波动；在这个测试规模下，我们无法将这些因素区分开来。Cerebras 是唯一的 fp16 端点，因此没有第二个 fp16 端点可供比较。

本次测试涵盖一天内的一个模型、280 道任务和六个端点。它并不能证明 4 位精度适用于所有模型或工作负载，因此在将流量转移到 4 位端点之前，请先测试你自己的提示词。

API 提供商提供哪些精度？

fp8 是最常见的已标注精度，而大多数端点根本没有报告精度。我们从端点 API 获取了每个模型的端点，返回结果共包含 470 个模型的 1,455 个端点。

865 个 unknown 端点中，有 610 个属于完全没有已标注端点的闭源权重模型，包括所有 Claude 和 Gemini 模型，以及除 gpt-oss 之外的所有 OpenAI 模型。其余 255 个端点中，253 个属于提供商未标注精度的开放权重模型。163 个拥有已标注端点的模型中，只有 54 个拥有 16 位端点，因此对大多数开放权重模型来说，8 位或 4 位是仅有的已标注选项。

量化端点更便宜吗？

通常如此，但并非总是如此。对每个模型，我们按输入 token 与输出 token 为三比一的混合价格，比较了各精度下最便宜的端点。

比较模型数较低精度更便宜差价在 2% 以内较低精度更贵价格比中位数
8 位与 16 位2414370.94

提供商对价格的影响比精度更大。对于同一精度下有多个端点的模型，最贵端点与最便宜端点的价格比中位数为 1.72。Qwen3.8 27B 的十个 fp8 端点价格介于每百万混合 token 0.342 美元至 1.137 美元之间。要将请求发送到符合精度筛选条件的最便宜端点，可在模型标识符后添加 :floor，具体见我们的最低成本推理指南。设置 quantizations: [“fp8”] 后，qwen/qwen3.8-27b:floor 在我们的两次尝试中都路由到了最便宜的 fp8 端点 Chutes。

在我们的测试中，完整运行 280 道任务的最低费用来自 fp4，最高费用来自 fp16，但中间的费用排序并不遵循精度。运行一遍的费用分别为 Darkbloom（fp4）0.58 美元、AkashML（fp8）0.72 美元、ModelRun（fp4）0.77 美元、Parasail（fp8）0.81 美元、CoreWeave（fp8）1.19 美元，以及 Cerebras（fp16）1.24 美元。速度也不遵循精度。Cerebras（fp16）和 ModelRun（fp4）的响应时间中位数分别为 1.3 秒和 2.4 秒，其他四个端点则为 8.4 至 15.0 秒。在所有端点中，除仅有一个端点的 fp32 外，各已标注精度的 24 小时可用率中位数均为 99.8% 或更高。

如何选择你获得的精度？

先查看模型各端点提供的精度，再在请求中设置 provider.quantizations。向 https://openrouter.ai/api/v1/models/qwen/qwen3.8-27b/endpoints 发送 GET 请求，会为每个端点返回一个条目，包含其量化格式、价格、上下文长度和可用率。我们调用时，无需 API 密钥就得到了响应，模型的提供商标签页也显示相同的列表。对于 Qwen3.8 27B，它列出了 21 个端点，包括一个 bf16、一个 fp16、十个 fp8、三个 fp4 和六个 unknown。在锁定精度前，请先查看所需精度的端点数量，因为这个数量决定了某个端点故障时有多少端点可以接替。

要让请求使用 8 位或更高精度，请列出你接受的精度。

import os
import requests

response = requests.post(
    "https://openrouter.ai/api/v1/chat/completions",
    headers={"Authorization": f"Bearer {os.environ['OPENROUTER_API_KEY']}"},
    json={
        "model": "qwen/qwen3.8-27b",
        "messages": [{"role": "user", "content": "What is the capital of Australia? One word."}],
        "reasoning": {"enabled": False},
        "provider": {"quantizations": ["fp8", "bf16", "fp16"]},
    },
    timeout=120,
)
data = response.json()
if "error" in data:
    raise RuntimeError(data["error"])
print(data["provider"], data["choices"][0]["message"]["content"], f'${data["usage"]["cost"]:.6f}')

我们运行了三次，每次都打印出相同的一行。

Reka Canberra $0.000007

提供商路由量化文档列出了所有可接受的值，并解释了 quantizations 如何与 only、order 和 sort 配合使用。

quantizations 会筛选端点列表。我们会移除所有精度不在列表中的端点，然后在其余端点之间进行负载均衡，按权重优先选择价格最低的端点，并在提供商故障时回退到下一个端点。这个筛选条件并不保证每次都使用同一家提供商，因此如果你要跟踪质量，请记录响应中的 provider 字段。文档还指出，fp4 包含 mxfp4 和 nvfp4，fp8 包含 mxfp8。

精度筛选的常见问题及解决方法

筛选在联系任何提供商之前执行，因此候选列表为空时会快速失败。请求 Qwen3.8 27B 使用没有任何端点提供的 int8 时，在 0.4 秒内返回了 404。

{"error":{"message":"No endpoints found for the request with quantization: int8. To learn more about provider routing, visit: https://openrouter.ai/docs/guides/routing/provider-selection","code":404,"metadata":{"routing_funnel":[{"step":"Initial Endpoints","endpoint_count":21}],"failed_routing_step":"Filter by Quantization"}}}

routing_funnel 字段显示每一步后剩余的端点数量，failed_routing_step 则指出哪一步使端点数量归零。{“quantizations”: [“fp8”], “only”: [“cerebras”]} 返回了相同的 404，并带有 quantization: fp8，因为 Cerebras 提供的是 fp16，所以漏斗中的端点数从 21 个变为 1 个，再变为零。

当只有一个端点匹配时，失败过程会更慢。Cerebras 是 Qwen3.8 27B 唯一的 fp16 端点。在我们的测试中，请求通过 allow_fallbacks: false 锁定到 Cerebras，最初的 280 个请求中，有 93 个连续三次失败，并出现以下错误（已节选）。

{"message":"Provider returned error","code":429,"metadata":{"raw":"qwen/qwen3.8-27b is temporarily rate-limited upstream. Please retry shortly, or add your own key to accumulate your rate limits: https://openrouter.ai/settings/integrations","provider_name":"Cerebras","limit_source":"upstream_provider_shared_pool","retry_after_seconds":59}}

我们不断重试，直到全部 280 个请求完成。单独设置 quantizations: [“fp16”] 也只会留下同一个候选端点，因此如果该端点触发速率限制，就没有其他端点可转向。将列表扩大为 [“fp16”, “bf16”] 后，路由器就有了第二个候选端点，同一个请求随后路由到了 DeepInfra。

提供商故障也可能伴随 HTTP 200 状态返回，因为提供商一接受请求，我们就会发送状态。请检查响应正文中是否存在 error，不要只检查状态码。

使用 Exacto 按质量信号对端点排序

量化后的质量取决于“所使用的方法”，而且各提供商运行各自的推理软件，因此即使两个端点的标签相同，也无法保证表现一致。对于带有工具的请求，Auto Exacto 已经会将吞吐量、工具调用成功率和基准测试得分较低的端点移到列表后面。要将这种排序应用于不带工具的请求，可在模型标识符后添加 :exacto。Exacto 根据工具调用信号对端点排序，而非根据其在你所执行任务上的准确率，因此请用你自己的提示词测试正在考虑的端点。如何评估 LLM 提供商的性能介绍了如何比较它们的延迟、吞吐量和可用率。

常见问题

量化位数更高还是更低更好？

更多位数能保留原始模型更多的精度，也会占用更多内存。在 2026 年 10 月 20 日对 Qwen3.8 27B 的测试中，我们在 240 道有确切答案的任务上，未检测到 fp8、fp4 和 fp16 端点之间的准确率差异。这只涵盖一天内的一个模型，因此在决定采用 4 位精度之前，请先在你自己的工作负载上测试。

为什么量化不会破坏 LLM 的准确率？

并非所有权重都同样重要。AWQ 发现，保护约 1% 最重要的权重可以大幅减少量化误差；LLM.int8() 则使用混合精度，将离群值保留为 16 位，同时对超过 99.9% 的数值使用 8 位进行乘法运算。我们对 Qwen3.8 27B 的测试无法表明提供商使用了哪些方法，但 fp16 端点在 240 道任务中答错了 3 道，fp8 和 fp4 端点则答错了 2 至 4 道。

什么时候应该量化模型？

当 16 位模型无法装入你的硬件，或者你需要用相同的 GPU 获得更高吞吐量时，可以进行量化。在我们的测试中，未检测到 fp8 带来的损失，而且 fp8 对每个权重的舍入幅度比 4 位更小，因此它是幅度更小的一步。无论选择哪一种，都请先在你自己的任务上测试。通过 API 使用时，你无需自行量化模型，而是通过 provider.quantizations，在 OpenRouter 上选择一个提供所需精度的端点。

提供商的量化格式标为“unknown”是什么意思？

这意味着提供商尚未报告该端点的精度。截至 2026 年 10 月 20 日，OpenRouter 的 1,455 个端点中有 865 个标为 unknown，其中 610 个属于 Claude 和 Gemini 等闭源权重模型。unknown 也是 provider.quantizations 接受的值，因此你可以包含或排除这些端点。
